---
title: "Figure conventions and reproducibility"
---

Documentation figures are drawn with **R and ggplot2**, from one shared theme in
`figures/style.R` and the figure jobs in `figures/render.R`. The walkthroughs
compute with Python and pass the points to R for drawing. The extension itself has
no graphics or R dependency.

## Visual conventions

- Language comparisons keep **R, Python, PHP** in that order. Python is labeled
  statsmodels or SciPy reference to identify the actual implementation.
- R uses blue circles (#0072B2); Python uses orange triangles (#D55E00); PHP uses
  green squares (#009E73). Color and shape reinforce the labels.
- Conceptual figures use blue for the reference/population curve, green for the
  conditional/native curve, orange for an approximation or boundary, and gray for
  observations. Their legends describe the statistical quantity rather than imply
  that a curve is an implementation comparison.
- Use a white background, common sans-serif type, restrained grids and explicit
  quantity/unit labels. Titles state what is shown; captions state the data or
  approximation, transformations and relevant limits.
- Bar charts start at zero. Benchmark facets use their own labeled linear scales
  and show median bars plus actual timing repetitions. Missing memory is labeled
  unrecorded, not plotted as measured zero. A measured time of zero is marked 0*
  because timer resolution can hide a short fit.
- Log scales are explicit and reserved for quantities spanning orders of magnitude,
  such as integration errors. The 1e-13 display floor in the quadrature-error plot
  is disclosed; it never changes stored numerical measurements.
- Error-versus-reference figures use a zero reference line and label any unit
  multiplier. Agreement plots are not residual or model-adequacy diagnostics.

Each figure is saved as an **SVG** with selectable text and a **160-dpi PNG**,
at fixed dimensions recorded in the [figure manifest](figures/manifest.json). The
font family is generic sans-serif, so the resolved font can differ across
platforms. The conventions use ggplot2's
[themes](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/theme.html) and
[export controls](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggsave.html).

## Generate figures without running fits or benchmarks

Install the documentation-only R packages:

```r
install.packages(c("ggplot2", "jsonlite", "svglite"),
                 repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
```

From the repository root:

```sh
Rscript docs/figures/render.R --all
# Or render an individual family/figure:
Rscript docs/figures/render.R ols
Rscript docs/figures/render.R approximation
Rscript docs/figures/render.R sleepstudy
./scripts/render-docs
```

- The renderer reads saved benchmark and reference reports and the points in
  `figures/data/`. It does not call estimators, regenerate fixtures, or run
  timings. Refresh the plots when a numerical report changes; a style change
  does not need new timings.
- Profile and posterior plots use points exported by the executable walkthroughs.
  Re-executing those pages updates their JSON point snapshots and figures.
- SVGs are embedded with namespaced clip IDs, so figures on one page do not
  interfere.
- An ordinary site render reuses frozen outputs and saved images. Re-executing
  the computational notebooks needs the [documentation environment](documentation.qmd).

The [manifest](figures/manifest.json) records each input's path and MD5, the image
hashes and dimensions, the renderer and theme hashes, the R version, the platform,
and the direct package versions. [The R package record](figures/r-packages.json)
adds the transitive dependency versions. Other versions may not reproduce the
figures byte for byte. The data's provenance stays in the verification records.

## Existing figure coverage

The renderer draws:

- the five fixed-effect and Gaussian random-intercept benchmarks, and the
  binomial mixed-model benchmark
- the v0.1 comparisons with earlier results
- Gaussian likelihood profiles, published-data agreement, and sleepstudy random
  slopes
- binomial mixed-model integration error, node sensitivity, and conditional
  posterior shape

SVG and PNG downloads are kept next to their input records.
